A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same catch-tag-release research, with matching authors, Phi-3 examples, and sequence-averaging construction. Their text, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation visualizations, pruning interventions, and MMLU few-shot measurements in Sections 2–3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original sink measurements, semantic-probe accuracies, model comparisons, synthetic training results, and supplementary analyses throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The original mechanism and two-layer construction remain, but v2 adds activation decomposition into tag/non-tag components and corresponding mass-mean probing procedures (Section 4). Appendix C introduces a two-separator model with three-dimensional embeddings, two heads per layer, and learned output projections, substantially extending the methodological content.

E1.justification: v2 removes MMLU evaluation and C4 pruning calibration. It adds city/country truth classification, SST-2 sentiment classification, QuALITY text analysis, and empirical synthetic averaging tasks, including a two-separator task. Several original qualitative prompting scenarios remain in the reorganized visualization appendix.

E2.justification: The evaluated OATS, Wanda, and SparseGPT comparisons in v1 disappear, along with their dense and low-rank-removal controls. v2 introduces comparisons between tag-only, non-tag, and full-activation mass-mean probes in Tables 1, 5, and 7. OATS remains cited but is no longer experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The removed pruning evaluation used 50% sparsity and 0–5-shot MMLU testing. New protocols include aggregation over 170 prompts truncated to 150 tokens, a sink threshold of 0.2, a tag-subspace projection metric, balanced 400/200 probe construction/validation splits, and synthetic-model training for 50 epochs. Model configurations also expand substantially.

E4.justification: v2 removes the low-rank deletion and pruning interventions. It adds sink-token taxonomies, tag-separability measurements, twelve-threshold sensitivity analysis, initialization sensitivity, and a multihead synthetic experiment (Appendices B–D, F, K). Comparisons across reasoning and QK-normalized models add further analyses; these are comparisons between checkpoints, not controlled architectural ablations.

E5.justification: v1 reports no repeated-run analysis. v2 Table 8 reports success frequencies across ten runs for each initialization. Figure 3 also explicitly defines distribution quartiles and percentile whiskers across heads; these describe heterogeneity rather than confidence intervals. Repeated-run uncertainty reporting remains localized.

E6.justification: v1's MMLU curves and pruning findings are removed. New results include 92.5–99.5% cities tag-probe accuracy (Table 1), average sink counts of 1.125 versus 2.196 for pretrained versus distilled Qwen 14B (Figure 5), sentiment accuracies, and initialization success rates of 4/10, 3/10, and 0/10 (Table 8). These are newly reported experiments, not matched-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The averaging theorem's parameter assumptions, convergence result, and most proof steps are retained, moving from v1 Section 4/Appendix A to v2 Section 7/Appendix E. Limited changes include corrected causal summation bounds and removal of explicit low-rank/outlier assertions from the theorem statement. v2 also formalizes sink/tag projections and decompositions, but supplies no new theorem for the multihead extension.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds low-rank parameter structure, compression benefits, and the claimed necessity of catch-tag-release for averaging. v2 instead foregrounds semantic information in tags, stronger manifestations in reasoning-distilled models, and persistence with QK normalization. Its theoretical claim is narrowed to a constructive solution and empirical emergence through training.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations involving semantic denoising, reasoning-related segmentation, tag orthogonality, activation steering, and MLP reinforcement of shared tags. Appendix K explicitly acknowledges that the mechanism is not proved necessary, optimization can fail, reasoning correlations are not causal evidence, and threshold-based detection is incomplete. These substantially qualify v1's stronger explanations.

D1.justification: v2 adds synthetic-data generation and optimization details, initialization and scheduling information, probe extraction layers/heads, a model inventory, and GPU/runtime estimates (Appendices G, J, L–M). It removes v1's pruning calibration/hyperparameter recipe and project-page link. These substantially revise the available reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The compression-focused literature discussion is substantially reduced. v2 adds or expands positioning around over-mixing, positional encodings, QK normalization, semantic probing, and activation steering (Sections 1.3 and 8; Appendix I). These changes go beyond publication updates to retained references such as OATS.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, research questions, contribution list, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around semantic and quantitative analysis. The pruning-centered narrative is replaced, the main proof moves into Appendix E, and the appendix structure is extensively reorganized. This is substantial narrative revision beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redesigns the retained mechanism/PCA displays, and removes pruning plots and activation-outlier panels. Numerous new violin plots, box plots, heatmaps, histograms, prompt diagrams, and result tables substantially change the visual presentation. Several original appendix examples are retained in compact, rearranged panels.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the mechanism's generality and semantic role through quantitative measurements, controlled probe comparisons, and sensitivity analyses. It also resolves v1's central overstatement of theoretical necessity by explicitly distinguishing a constructive solution from necessity and acknowledging optimization failures. Removing the pruning/MMLU evidence and project-page link sacrifices practical evidence and access information, but the broader empirical support and better-calibrated conclusions provide a substantial net improvement.
